solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group of people's second-rate in test

definitions.note: a possessive phrase, matching the adjective's sense of belonging to a tribe

indicators.note: the grade letter is placed inside the word for an examination

parts.note: a trial is a test
B is the second grade, after A

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a group of people did poorly in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes what belongs to a tribe, a group of people sharing descent or culture.

clue.text: Herb that is submerged under butter

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits lower, beneath the first

parts.note: a ram is an animal that butts, a butter
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A culinary herb sunk beneath a knob of butter in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but something that butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramie is a nettle-family plant grown for its fibre, loosely a herb or herbaceous plant.

clue.text: Grumbler who doesn't manage with an incisive type?

definitions.meaning: a carping critic who speaks ill of people behind their backs

definitions.text: who doesn't manage with an incisive type?
definitions.meaning: someone not chewing with front incisors bites with the rear teeth instead

explanation.surface: A moaner described as someone who can't cope with sharp-minded people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incisive' looks like 'sharp-witted' but points to incisors, the front teeth, so the second reading is a person who bites with the back teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A backbiter is a malicious gossip, a carping complainer about others.

clue.text: Someone getting too hot may want this reading

definitions.text: Someone getting too hot may want this
definitions.meaning: an overheated person wants fewer clothes worn
a passage read aloud in church services

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as LESS ON: an overheated person wants fewer garments.
explanation.definitionFit: In church a lesson is a scripture passage read out during the service.

clue.text: They'll go to work at last? Nonsense!

definitions.text: They'll go to work at last?
definitions.meaning: shoe menders work on a last, the foot-shaped block

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the claim that some idlers will finally get to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' seems to mean 'finally'; a last is the foot-shaped block shoe menders work on. 'Cobblers!' is British slang for 'rubbish!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoe repairers are cobblers, and the word is also British slang for rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Wobbly customer is grey, about a hundred? This may improve appearance

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the Roman numeral
unsteady, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: An unsteady, grey-haired client nearing a hundred might want a smartening up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About a hundred' looks like an age; 'about' is a container signal and the hundred is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic operations exist to alter and enhance how a person looks.

clue.text: Maybe people on river will catch fifty fish

indicators.note: the river folk hold the numeral within them

parts.note: boaters are people out in boats, for example on a river
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Anglers on a river expect to land fifty fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are herrings cured by salting and smoking, so a kind of fish.

clue.text: A mistake having drinks with drug

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks with its tongue
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Mixing drinks with drugs is described as an error of judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or brief failure, a synonym for a mistake.

clue.text: Official is back to grasp the heart of the matter, right?

indicators.note: the word for the back holds the core idea in its grip

parts.note: the rear is the back
the gist is the essential point

explanation.surface: An official is urged to get back to the core issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like 'return' but is REAR, which takes in GIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is an official keeping records such as births, marriages and deaths.

clue.text: Saints receiving ridicule for rustic garments?

indicators.note: the two letters for saints take in the word for ridicule

parts.note: to mock is to ridicule

explanation.surface: Holy figures are mocked for wearing peasant clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocks are loose overgarments traditionally worn by farm labourers.

clue.text: Arrest head servant by front of stable

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word stable is taken

parts.note: top means head, as in the top of the table
a page is a young servant

explanation.surface: A chief servant is arrested beside the stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head servant' reads as one job title, but 'head' and 'servant' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrest of movement or flow is a stoppage, a halt.

clue.text: European politician returning without money for college

indicators.note: the politician's letters come back in reverse order

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
broke means having no money

explanation.surface: A Euro-MP goes home penniless and turns to a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Pembroke is the name of colleges at both Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Belief is held by those folk

indicators.note: the plural pronoun holds the little word inside

parts.note: them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A belief is said to be held by a particular group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods, a religious conviction.

clue.text: Declamation from worker against queen?

indicators.note: next to, so the royal letter is set beside the insect

parts.note: R stands for Regina, queen
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A speech from a worker protesting against the monarch, or against a queen insect.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker and queen both suggest a bees' or ants' colony, but they are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rant is a loud, impassioned speech, a kind of declamation.

clue.text: That ore in ground, a rare feldspar

indicators.note: crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A rare mineral is found in some ore after it has been crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorthite is the calcium-rich end member of the plagioclase feldspar series, uncommon in pure form.

clue.text: Thus boy becomes yob by way of retaliation?

definitions.meaning: the word boy written backwards gives yob

explanation.surface: A lad turns thug as an act of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: YOB is BOY read backwards, the origin of the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as a payback or repayment for an injury is doing it as retaliation.

clue.text: Obsession about attending church, getting a job in the country?

indicators.note: the word for an obsession goes around the other letters

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it
at means attending, as in at school

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on churchgoing finds work in a rural parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofing with straw or reed is a traditional rural trade.

clue.text: Boring race that gives no decisive result

definitions.note: a phrase standing for something that ends without a winner

parts.note: dead can mean dull or lifeless
a heat is a qualifying race

explanation.surface: A dull race finishes with nobody clearly winning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie in which competitors finish exactly level produces no single winner.

clue.text: Students away from home? They are about to go on a cruise maybe

definitions.meaning: pupils living at a boarding school

definitions.text: They are about to go on a cruise maybe

explanation.surface: Students away from home are pictured setting off on a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils who live in at school, and people getting onto a ship, both go by this word.

clue.text: Astronomer Royal being offhand

definitions.meaning: George Biddell ... held that British post from 1835 to 1881

explanation.surface: A royal astronomer is described as dismissive.
explanation.definitionFit: George Airy was Astronomer Royal; separately, an airy manner is light and casual.

clue.text: Female secures what a shepherdess must secure?

parts.note: locks means fastens or secures

explanation.surface: A woman fastens something, as a shepherdess must keep her animals safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of sheep are what a shepherdess keeps penned and safe.

clue.text: Silly dispute almost resolved

indicators.note: settled or worked out afresh, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the word dispute loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A foolish quarrel is nearly settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims DISPUTE to DISPUT, which 'resolved' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and silly are close synonyms for foolish.

clue.text: Platforms for foot treatment go missing

indicators.note: the word for a go is absent from the longer word

parts.note: podiatry is the care and treatment of feet
a try is a go or attempt

explanation.surface: A sign warns that a platform for foot care has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia is the plural of podium, a raised stand or dais.

clue.text: Move to get old king back in charge

indicators.note: the reversed name sits within the word for a charge

parts.note: a rate is a charge or price

indicators.note: the old king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch is restored to power.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the nursery-rhyme king; 'back' turns COLE to ELOC.
explanation.definitionFit: To move, as house or office, is to relocate to a new place.

clue.text: Monster to walk with head concealed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a walk is hidden away

parts.note: a stroll is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: A creature walks about with its head covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is an ugly giant or dwarf of Scandinavian folklore, a monster.

clue.text: Like a sort of view offered by food manufacturer

definitions.meaning: a view from high above is a panoramic one

explanation.surface: A food company offers a particular perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's-eye view is seen from above; Birds Eye is a frozen-food brand known for fish fingers.

clue.text: Tunic in fashion provided by Greek character

indicators.note: the fashion word comes after, supplied by the Greek letter

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ton means high fashion or style

explanation.surface: A fashionable tunic supplied by someone Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiton was the long woollen or linen tunic of ancient Greece.

clue.text: A new attempt by number who may be dealing with landlord?

definitions.text: who may be dealing with landlord?

parts.note: ten is a number
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Several people make a fresh attempt at negotiating with their landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is TEN; the order is TEN, A, N, TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenantry means tenants collectively, the people who rent from a landlord.

clue.text: Showing wisdom and cunning? About time!

indicators.note: the word for cunning goes around the word for a period

parts.note: sly means cunning
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a wise and crafty move has come at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as impatience, but 'About' is the container signal and 'time' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To act sagely is to act wisely, like a sage.
